absent: Leaf handlers for cleaning records and write protection are not in these fragments, so their dirty tracking and permission changes are unknown.
Middle level directory handling for huge pages is not in these fragments, so its splitting and warning rules are unknown.
Core page range walk engine and operation safety checks are not in these fragments, so traversal order and error propagation beyond clipping are unknown.
Folio reference counting helpers and huge page pud predicates are not in these fragments, so pin detection edge cases are unknown.
Extended array iteration and scheduling constants plus cache and translation flush primitives are not in these fragments, so their exact ordering guarantees are unknown.
Backing store operations for shared memory and huge pages plus quota and security initialization are not in these fragments, so file creation side effects beyond shown steps are unknown.
Memory policy mode operations plus node mask scratch handling plus cache lifetimes are not in these fragments, so policy creation failures beyond validation are unknown.
System control scope values and huge encoding layout and name length limits are not fully defined here, so numeric boundary behavior is unknown.

findings.text: A helper exposed for shared file ranges takes a mapping plus a start index and length, holds mapping read protection across a page table walk with write protect operations, and returns a total count accumulated in private walk state.

A helper exposed for shared file ranges takes a mapping plus range plus bitmap placement plus bitmap storage plus result bounds, initializes result bounds to empty when input bounds are empty, holds mapping read protection across a page table walk with cleaning operations, then writes back observed bounds and returns a total count.

A mapping walk helper takes a mapping plus start index plus length plus operation table plus private data, rejects unsafe operation tables, asserts mapping lock is held, iterates virtual areas overlapping the range, clips range to each area, converts page offsets to addresses, skips empty clips, runs a per area test then a range walk, and stops on first error with positive test meaning stop without error.
A file control entry supports two commands, one to add seals and one to query seals, delegating to dedicated seal helpers and rejecting any other command as invalid.

A creation helper builds an anonymous file by name and flags, choosing huge page backing when requested and shared memory backing otherwise, initializes anonymous security state, enables seek and read and write modes with large file handling, then adjusts mode bits and initial seals for no execute seal or allow sealing cases.
A setup helper forwards name plus size plus flags to an internal shared memory constructor bound to the shared memory mount with no extra inode flags.
Page walk filtering reads area flags once and processes only areas that are shared and possibly writable while skipping huge table areas and all other flag combinations.

At the upper directory level the walk leaves huge entries unsplit and simply continues, while warning if such an entry appears writable or dirty, with behavior compiled only where architectural huge pud support exists.
Clipped page range bounds are translated to addresses by subtracting area base page offset, scaling by page size, and adding area start address, preserving empty range skipping.

Before scanning an area the walk resets flush bounds to an empty inverted interval, opens a protection notification range over the area bounds, starts invalidation, flushes caches, and marks translation flush pending without recording a full gather range. After scanning it flushes either the full notified range under nesting or only the tracked dirty subrange when nonempty, then ends notification and clears pending state.
Both shared range helpers acquire mapping read protection before walking and release it after, and the mapping walk itself requires that same protection to be held by the caller.

Two operation tables share the same directory level handlers and the same test plus pre plus post hooks, differing only at the leaf level where one table records cleaning state and the other applies write protection.
A folio is considered pinned when its observed reference count differs from its expected count.

Pin tagging drains least recently used additions, holds interrupt protected extended array state across a full scan, marks entries that are not values and show extra references, and periodically pauses state, releases protection, yields the processor, and reacquires protection to bound latency.

Pin waiting first tags candidates then scans up to a fixed number of passes, exiting early when no marks remain, draining globally on first pass and sleeping with growing delay on later passes where an interruptible sleep aborts to the final pass, clearing marks for unpinned entries and reporting busy only if pinned entries survive to the final pass while always clearing final marks.
Seal storage is located from shared memory inode state for shared memory files and from huge page inode state for huge page files where supported, otherwise no storage exists.

Seal addition requires write mode and only known seal bits, serializes on the inode, rejects unknown file types and any addition after sealing of seal changes, expands execute seal into shrink plus grow plus write plus future write seals when execute bits are present, and for newly added write seal denies future writable mappings then waits for pins with rollback of the denial on failure before committing new bits.
Seal query returns current bits when seal storage exists and invalid otherwise.

Write sealed state is defined as presence of either write seal or future write seal. Private mappings ignore writability checks. Shared mappings with write permission are rejected when write sealed, while shared read only mappings are allowed but stripped of future writability.

Flag sanitizing rejects unknown bits, allows huge size encoding only with huge request, rejects simultaneous execute and no execute seal requests, then applies system control defaults for execute versus no execute seal.

When neither execute nor no execute seal is requested, system control scope selects a default, and enforcement scope rejects creation without no execute seal while emitting a rate limited diagnostic naming the task and scope value.
Name allocation reserves fixed maximum length, copies a fixed prefix, appends user bytes bounded to remaining capacity, and fails on copy fault or overlong input with cleanup.

Shared memory construction rejects bad mounts, negative or oversized sizes, and identity mapped mounts, accounts size unless no reserve is set with rollback on later failure, creates an unlinked regular inode, expands mapping where needed, and wraps the inode as a read write pseudo file with shared memory operations, releasing the inode on failure.
Size accounting is skipped entirely when no reserve is set, otherwise it charges the current address space and uncharges symmetrically on release.

New shared memory inodes receive a reserved number, owned identity, zero blocks, fresh timestamps and random generation, zeroed private area with locked list heads and eviction controls, default sealed against further seal changes, no reserve propagated from flags, inherited filesystem flags where applicable, unevictable and large folio mapping options from superblock state, and type specific operations with shared policy initialized for regular files and directories and links.
Shared memory inode creation initializes quota then allocates quota, dropping quota and marking no quota with inode release on either failure.

Shared policy initialization starts with an empty tree and initialized lock, and when a mount policy is supplied it creates a file scoped policy from mode plus flags plus user mask, contextualizes the mask under task lock, and inserts a single node covering the whole file range while managing references and scratch storage.

Policy creation treats default mode as no policy with empty mask required, maps preferred with empty mask to local unless static or relative flags forbid it, rejects local with nonempty mask or static or relative flags, rejects other modes with empty mask, and otherwise allocates with single reference plus mode plus flags plus no home node.

Node mask setting bypasses absent or local policies, intersects current allowed memory nodes with online memory state, folds relative masks onto allowed sets or intersects direct masks, records either user mask or current allowed set depending on flags, then delegates to mode specific creation.

Shared policy nodes store start plus end plus policy, allocation duplicates the policy with shared marking and rolls back on failure, initialization assigns bounds and policy, and insertion orders by start then end in a balanced tree and halts on overlap.
Overlapping policy node insertion is fatal, huge directory entries observed writable or dirty trigger warnings, and mapping walk failures trigger warnings while still returning accumulated totals.
A killable sleep during pin waiting forces remaining passes to be skipped to the final cleanup pass, and final pass converts surviving pins into a busy error rather than retaining marks.
Maximum pin wait scan index equals 4, documented as bounding total delay near one hundred fifty milliseconds.
Pinned tag constant aliases PAGECACHE_TAG_TOWRITE.
Aggregate seal mask combines seal plus exec plus shrink plus grow plus write plus future write variants.
Aggregate creation flag mask combines close on exec plus allow sealing plus huge table plus no exec seal plus exec variants.
Anonymous file name prefix spells memfd with trailing colon, its length excludes termination, and maximum user suffix length equals system name limit minus prefix length.

Each pin wait scan holds interrupt protected extended array state across marked entries only, with the same periodic pause plus release plus yield plus reacquire pattern and final release after the scan.

Write protect walk private state carries a running total, flush interval bounds, and a notification range. Cleaning walk private state extends that with bitmap placement plus bitmap storage plus result bounds.
Whether user mask is retained depends on user mask flag bits, and relative mask conversion folds the original mask by weight of the relative set then maps it onto that set.
